text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-INC-7421 — metrics/logs ingestion: kafka.consumer_lag > 10m for log-topic-prod (severity: P1). Trigger: consumer_lag > 600000ms on consumer-group=logstash-prod-consumers. links: https://pagerduty.example/PD-INC-7421

Kiran Patel: ack’ing and joining. I’m oncall. pulling context now — can someone paste the PD runbook if handy?

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by Kiran Patel at 2026-03-14T20:01:12Z. On-call escalation policy: primary -> secondary in 12 minutes if not resolved.

Maya Chen: saw dashboard spike in kafka_consumergroup_lag about ~650k ms across partitions 3-9. Also seeing a sharp drop in log ingestion throughput on logstash pods in us-west-2. Looks like backpressure rather than broker down.

Jorge Alvarez: grep on brokers shows disk I/O high on broker-7. Possible GC spikes on broker too. throwing some logs below:
```
[2026-03-14T19:58:01Z] broker-7 WARN DiskScheduler: write stall detected 1200ms
[2026-03-14T19:59:25Z] broker-7 INFO GC: pausetimes: 1100ms young, 2400ms full
[2026-03-14T19:59:59Z] broker-7 ERROR NetworkProcessor: request handler slow 900ms
```

Priya Singh: copying quick triage steps from runbook: 1) check consumer lag (kafka-consumer-groups.sh) 2) check logstash backpressure (kubectl logs -l app=logstash -n prod) 3) verify disk pressure on brokers (iostat) 4) consider increasing consumer parallelism or throttling producers.

Kiran Patel: running consumer group check now. output snippet:
```
$ kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --describe --group logstash-prod-consumers
TOPIC           PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG
log-topic-prod  3          124050000       124700500       650500
log-topic-prod  4          123900100       124530300       630200
... (multiple partitions > 600k)
```
Lag is across many partitions. Not just a single stuck consumer.

Maya Chen: probable cause: burst of producer traffic + broker-7 IO and a paused consumer pool. Suggest first mitigation: scale logstash consumers by 2x and temporarily enable fetch.min.bytes reduction to drain backlog faster. Also put an ingress throttle for noisy source api-search-prod for 10m.

Jorge Alvarez: I can SSH to broker-7 and check disk and GC. If disk full / high iowait, we should move partitions off broker-7. Starting iostat and df now.

Jorge Alvarez: iostat shows iowait ~45%. df shows /var/lib/kafka at 78% used. GC logs consistent with long pauses. I’m going to trigger a broker rollover for high-lag partitions to other brokers (reassign-partitions). Will notify 2nd oncall before any partition moves.

Priya Singh: I’ll scale logstash replica count from 4 -> 8 in the prod namespace and restart the failing pods to pick up new consumer assignments. command: `kubectl scale deploy/logstash --replicas=8 -n prod`

Kiran Patel: executing scale. NOTE: we need to be careful about memory on pods — scaling is CPU-bound though. Also enabling temporary producer throttle on api-search-prod via API gateway rule (Maya, can you push?).

Maya Chen: pushing throttle rule now: rate-limit api-search-prod to 200 rps for 10m. applied.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-7421 updated: acknowledged by Kiran Patel. Timeline: 2026-03-14T20:02:10Z.

Priya Singh: logstash scaled to 8, new pods coming up. restarting stuck pods that reported backpressure.

Kiran Patel: monitoring lag. running a quick promql to track consumer lag per minute:
```
max_over_time(kafka_consumergroup_lag{group="logstash-prod-consumers"}[5m])
```
Showing drop from ~650k to ~300k in the last 8 minutes — good directional.

Jorge Alvarez: partition reassign started for the worst partitions away from broker-7. will post reassignment id and ETA.

incident-bot: Automatic escalation check: if lag not < 100k within 20m, auto-escalate to SRE Lead. Current state: lag trending down; escalation timer paused due to active mitigation.

Maya Chen: quick customer-impact note: ingestion lag means customers querying recent logs (last 10m) may get incomplete results for search & metrics dashboards. A subset of enterprise customers with strict ingestion SLOs will be impacted. We should open a bridge and notify CSMs.

Kiran Patel: creating postmortem ticket and bridge. bridge link: https://meet.example/bridge/PD-7421. CSM ping queued to #customer-success.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty note: PD-INC-7421: 2nd responder (Jorge Alvarez) added to incident.

Priya Singh: after restart & scale, consumer lag now ~80k on average, with some partitions ~110k. Still draining but much better. continuing to monitor.

Kiran Patel: good. keep watch for broker-7 health post reassign. Jorge, any risk of interrupted replicas?

Jorge Alvarez: replica move completed for 3 partitions, remaining 6 in progress. replication lag is normal. no ISR shrinks. risk minimal.

Maya Chen: can we keep ingress throttle in place for another 5m to let the pipeline stabilize?

Kiran Patel: yes leave throttle until we hit <50k lag sustained for 3m.

Oncall Rotation: handoff reminder — next oncall (Priya) will take ownership at 21:00 UTC. Kiran will update handoff notes.

Kiran Patel: summary for handoff (to include in incident ticket):
- timeline: PD fired at 20:00 UTC for kafka consumer lag >10m
- root cause hypothesis: broker-7 IO/GC causing consumer group stalls during a producer traffic spike; backlog accumulation across partitions
- mitigations applied: scaled logstash 4->8, restarted stuck pods, applied temporary ingress throttle for noisy producers, started partition reassignment away from broker-7
- current status: consumer lag reduced from ~650k -> ~80k and continuing to drain; replication reassignments in progress; broker-7 under investigation for GC/disk tuning
- customer impact: delayed log/metric ingestion for recent 5-15 minutes for affected tenants; CSM notified; no data loss reported
- next steps: finish reassignment, verify consumer lag <50k, remove throttle, revert logstash scale to baseline after stable, schedule follow-up postmortem with storage/infra teams

Priya Singh: taking over oncall at 21:00 UTC; I’ll stay on the bridge and follow through. tagging SRE Lead @Kelsey (not in channel) to loop in after initial fix.

incident-bot: Incident PD-INC-7421 status: mitigated -> monitoring. last update 2026-03-14T20:12:01Z. escalation disabled.

Kiran Patel: closing this thread for now, will update ticket with full logs and commands used. If lag creeps back up, reopen and page. thanks team :thumbsup:

Maya Chen: thanks all. postmortem draft after tomorrow.

Jorge Alvarez: leaving notes on broker-7 I/O: consider increasing disk throughput, tune GC flags, and revisit partition placement to avoid hotspots.

Priya Singh: handoff accepted. I’ll post final status at 21:05 UTC.

pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-7421 resolved (mitigated) at 2026-03-14T20:14:05Z.

Kiran Patel: final note: no customer complaints so far, CSMs are monitoring. allocating action items in the ticket for infra to investigate broker GC/disk config.

Priya Singh: final check: consumer lag sustained <40k for 10 minutes, removing throttle in 1 minute.

Oncall Rotation: handoff complete.
